source.prompt: Instrumental background music for a classic 1990s-style Japanese fantasy role-playing game. The writing and orchestration evoke the golden age of 16-bit console RPG soundtracks (memorable singable lead melody, clear bass line, warm chords, tasteful hall reverb), but the production is high quality, warm and full, recorded with real-sounding instruments. Completely original melody. The game's world lives in an endless night lit by lanterns, lamps and great beacon fires; the score is gentle and melancholic, with warmth and a quiet, stubborn hope. A northern snow village whose buried houses are linked by snow tunnels, glowing ice lanterns at every tunnel mouth, villagers preparing a winter-solstice bonfire festival while a blizzard howls outside. Cozy, hearth-warm and communal, with a hint of worry beneath the warmth. A singable fiddle waltz melody over a drone, like people humming by a fire. Tempo 84 BPM, 3/4 time, key of G major. Instrumentation: folk fiddle lead, nyckelharpa-like bowed drones, wooden flute answer, soft hand-played frame drum, warm cello and upright bass, gentle celesta sparkles like falling snow. Form: 4-bar drone and celesta intro; section A fiddle waltz melody; section B wooden flute answers in E minor, a little wistful; section A returns with cello countermelody; the last bar leads back to section A. Duration: 95 seconds. Instrumental only: no vocals, no singing, no spoken words, no lyrics. Keep one steady tempo and key from start to finish, no fade-in and no fade-out, no long silences; the last bar leads naturally back into the first bar so the piece loops seamlessly as game background music.
